name: Authyo OTP for Everest Forms
author: Konceptwise Digital Media Pvt Ltd

sections.description:
Authyo OTP for Everest Forms adds one-time password (OTP) verification via email and phone number to your forms, using Authyo’s secure delivery service. It supports SMS, WhatsApp, and voice call channels for phone verification, helping ensure that only verified users can submit Everest Forms and reducing spam while enhancing form security.

Features:
– Email and Phone OTP verification fields for Everest Forms
– Per-form switch: choose which forms use OTP from the plugin settings, and their standard Email and Phone fields are verified automatically
– Default country setting for phone numbers
– Support for SMS, WhatsApp, and Voice Call OTP (Voice Call India only)
– Secure one-time password handling
– Seamless integration with Authyo service
– Easy setup and configuration
– Fail-Safe Lead Protection (on by default, can be turned off): if your Authyo wallet balance runs out, forms keep accepting submissions so no leads are lost, and you get an email about it.
– Built-in limits on how often codes can be sent, to protect your Authyo balance from abuse

This plugin helps reduce spam and ensures that only verified users can submit your forms.

Note: OTP verification requires valid Authyo API credentials and sufficient wallet balance. If the balance runs out and Fail-Safe Lead Protection is on, submissions proceed without OTP verification to prevent lead loss; turn the switch off in Settings to block them instead.

Company Information

Important: This plugin is NOT affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially supported by Everest Forms. It is an independent third-party integration that works with Everest Forms to provide OTP functionality using Authyo’s API services.

External Services

This plugin connects to the Authyo API to send and verify one-time passwords (OTPs) for form submissions.

Service used: Authyo (https://app.authyo.io)
Purpose: To send and verify one-time passwords for Everest Forms forms.
Data sent: The email address or phone number entered by the user, the one-time code they type, your Authyo Client ID and Client Secret, and your site’s address (scheme and domain only) are transmitted securely to Authyo’s servers only for the purpose of OTP verification and to match the request to your registered domain.
When: Data is sent when the user requests an OTP and again when verifying it.
Provider: Authyo.
Terms of Service: https://authyo.io/terms-service
Privacy Policy: https://authyo.io/privacy-policy

Optional activation / deactivation notice (opt-in): The plugin settings have a consent checkbox that is unticked by default. Nothing described in this paragraph is sent unless you tick it. If you tick it and save your Client ID, the plugin tells Authyo (https://app.authyo.io/api/v1/user/WordpressWebhook) when the plugin is activated or deactivated on your site.
Data sent only in that case: the event (activated or deactivated), your site address, the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions, your Authyo Client ID and a timestamp. Your Client Secret, form entries, visitor data and admin email addresses are never sent.
When: when you save your Client ID with the box ticked, when the plugin is re-activated, and when it is deactivated. Unticking the box stops all further notices.

Dependencies

This plugin requires the Everest Forms plugin to be installed and activated.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/authyo-otp-for-everest-forms/ directory, or install through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Configure your Authyo Client ID and Client Secret in the plugin’s settings page under Authyo OTP.
  4. Open the Forms tab in the plugin settings and switch on the forms you want to protect. Their normal Email and Phone fields are then verified with OTP. Or add the “Authyo Email” or “Authyo Phone” field to a form from the General Fields section.
  5. Save and test your form.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require Everest Forms?

Yes. This is an extension for Everest Forms.

Which OTP methods are supported?

This plugin supports Email, SMS, WhatsApp, and Voice Call OTP verification. Note that Voice Call is currently available exclusively for India.

Is an Authyo account required?

Yes, you need an Authyo account and API credentials to use the service.

My site is behind Cloudflare or a load balancer and visitors get “Too many attempts”.

Code requests are limited per visitor. If your host does not pass on the visitor’s real IP address, every visitor looks the same and shares one limit. Ask your host to restore the real IP, or return it with the authyo_evf_client_ip filter.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4

  • New: Forms tab. Switch OTP on per form and its normal Email and Phone fields get verified (off by default).
  • New: setup progress bar and a “Send a test OTP” tool that sends and verifies a real code.
  • New: Default Country setting and a redesigned settings page.
  • New: optional consent checkbox (unticked by default) to tell Authyo when the plugin is activated or deactivated. See External Services.
  • New: warning when your Authyo wallet balance is low.
  • Improved: only Client ID and Client Secret are needed now (App ID is no longer asked for).
  • Improved: the send button shows how the code is delivered (WhatsApp, SMS or Voice Call). “Allow visitor to choose method” is on by default for new installs.
  • Security: API errors no longer expose credentials, the saved secret is no longer printed on the page, and a form can only be submitted with the email or phone that was verified.
  • Fix: “Allow Skip” now works, and forms are no longer blocked when Authyo is not configured, no phone channel is on, or OTP is not used for a standard Email field.
  • Fix: a phone number is only ever sent by SMS, WhatsApp or Voice Call, never by Email. On Everest Forms phone fields with the country flag, the code now goes to the flag country (no second country box).
  • Security: codes can only be requested for fields of live forms that use OTP, with a wait between codes and limits per number, visitor and site. A used verification cannot be used again, saved keys are now encrypted with a stronger method (old keys keep working), and a “Remove my saved keys” option was added.
  • Fix: works with cached pages, after a form is reset, and does not slow the page down when Authyo’s country list is unavailable. The scripts now load only on pages that show an Authyo field.
  • Your site address is now sent to Authyo with each request to match your registered domain. See External Services.

1.0.3

  • The form shortcode is now shown below the result after creating a new form or adding Authyo fields to an existing form in the setup wizard, with a one-click copy button.

1.0.2

  • Added a guided setup wizard that configures the whole integration from one popup.
  • Added a “Setup Authyo” button to the settings page.
  • Setup wizard steps: credentials, verification channels, countries, OTP behaviour and form setup.
  • Added the ability to add Authyo fields to an existing Everest Form, or create a new form with those fields, without leaving the popup.
  • Added Enable Authyo OTP, Default Country Code and Sender ID settings.
  • Redesigned the setup interface.

1.0.1

  • Fixed missing translators comment for i18n compliance.
  • Added Tested up to and Requires PHP headers to plugin file.

1.0.0

  • Initial release with Email and Phone OTP support for Everest Forms.
